problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ is a partition of the interval $[-1,1]$

- ${P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}}$ is a partition of the interval $[-1,1]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}10({y}_{j}+{y}_{j-1})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Double Sum Over a Rectangular Partition Using a Difference of Squares
examples.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- $P_1 = \left\{x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_m\right\}$ is a partition of the interval $[4, 6]$

- $P_2 = \left\{y_0, y_1, \ldots, y_n\right\}$ is a partition of the interval $[2, 6]$

Calculate  $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (x_i + x_{i-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j,$ where $\Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1}$ and $\Delta y_j = y_j - y_{j-1}.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ is a partition of the interval $[0,2]$

- ${P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}}$ is a partition of the interval $[1,6]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we can write the summation as

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ and ${\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}$ are just the lengths of the intervals $[0,2]$ and $[1,6]$ respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =2-0=2, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =6-1=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining our results, we have

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}=2\cdot 5=10.
$$
